subject: Output of selected taxonomic ranks for sequences in taxmap object

messages.author: 7adbaedb15b29d65
messages.subject: Output of selected taxonomic ranks for sequences in taxmap object
parts:
Hi all,

I was wondering if there is a relatively easy way to output selected taxonomic ranks for each sequence in a taxmap object?

for example I might want only " kingdom;phylum;class;order;family;genus;species " to be output for all sequences without un-ranked levels or sub-ranks such as sub-families, sub-orders...etc.

I see how I can make a table of the table of the taxonomy data and observation data with the taxonomy_data() and obs_data() functions and link the "hierarchies" with the "obs_taxon_ids" and only print out my approved ranks but I was wondering if there is a dedicated function for this or a more elegant solution?

Thanks in advance for any help and thanks to the developers of this package as well.


all the best,
Royce

messages.author: 565fb8e7abc16eb0
messages.subject: Re: Output of selected taxonomic ranks for sequences in taxmap object
parts:
Hi Royce,

Without seeing your data I cant say for sure, but I can imagine a few strategies, depend on whether you want to filter the object, or just add a column  in the obs_data table without filtering. There is no dedicated function to do this kind of thing yet, but I have some in mind that probably will be added in the next big update.

Both strategies use the `supertaxa` function, which returns the supertaxa for each taxon. You can make the function return taxon indexes (for `taxon_data`) using `index = TRUE` and include the target taxon in the list by `include_input = TRUE`. This is what we will be looping over:

library(metacoder)
supertaxa(unite_ex_data_1, index = TRUE, include_input = TRUE)

note that `unite_ex_data_1` is an included data set, so you can try this code.

Filtering taxa by rank:

data <- unite_ex_data_1
allowed_ranks <- c("kingdom", "phylum", "class",  "order", "family", "genus", "species")
data <- filter_taxa(data, rank %in% allowed_ranks)
data <- mutate_taxa(data, all_ranks = sapply(supertaxa(data, index = TRUE, include_input = TRUE),
                                             function(i) paste0(data$taxon_data$rank[rev(i)], collapse = ";")))


Only use some ranks, but dont filter:

data <- unite_ex_data_1
allowed_ranks <- c("kingdom", "phylum", "class",  "order", "family", "genus", "species")
data <- mutate_taxa(data, all_ranks = sapply(supertaxa(data, index = TRUE, include_input = TRUE),
                                             function(i) {
                                                 valid_ranks <- data$taxon_data$rank[rev(i)]
                                                 valid_ranks <- valid_ranks[valid_ranks %in% allowed_ranks]
                                                 paste0(valid_ranks, collapse = ";")
                                             }))


Mapping back to observations:

After either method, you can map the taxon data to the observations like so:

data$obs_data$all_ranks <- data$taxon_data$all_ranks[match(data$obs_data$obs_taxon_ids, data$taxon_data$taxon_ids)]

Hope this helps. Let me know if you have more questions or ideas for functions you would like to be added.

messages.subject: Re: Output of selected taxonomic ranks for sequences in taxmap object
parts:
Thank you so much Zachary, that helped a lot. I was not clear that I wanted the actual taxonomic rank names ('Metazoa' rather than  'Kingdom' for example) so I just changed 'rank' to 'name' (see highlight below) which ultimately enabled me to accomplish what I wanted, which was to write a fasta file with the seqinr package containing the taxonomic lineage in the fasta headers.

cheers,
Royce

##################################################################
data <- genbank_ex_data

allowed_ranks <- c("kingdom", "phylum", "class", 
                   "order", "family", "genus", "species")

data <- filter_taxa(data, rank %in% allowed_ranks)

data <- mutate_taxa(data, all_ranks = sapply(supertaxa(data,
              index = TRUE, include_input = TRUE),

function(i) paste0(data$taxon_data$name[rev(i)],
              collapse = ";")))
